question: Which Indian state celebrates Rongali Bihu, a spring dramatic-cultural festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rongali Bihu, also known as Bohag Bihu, is the most celebrated festival in Assam, marking the Assamese New Year.
 
• It is celebrated in April, usually around the 13th to 15th of the month, and marks the beginning of the Assamese calendar year.
 
• The festival lasts for several days and includes various cultural activities such as traditional dance (Bihu dance), music, and feasting.
 
• Rongali Bihu is a spring festival that signifies the arrival of spring and the agricultural season, reflecting the agrarian culture of Assam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu Festival Types:**

 
 
• There are three primary Bihu festivals in Assam: Rongali or Bohag Bihu (spring festival), Kongali or Kati Bihu (autumn festival), and Bhogali or Magh Bihu (winter festival).
 
• Each of these festivals marks a significant phase in the Assamese agricultural calendar.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Attire:**
 
 
• During Rongali Bihu, people wear traditional Assamese attire. Women wear mekhela chador, and men wear dhotis and gamusas.
 
• These garments are often adorned with traditional motifs and are usually handwoven.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Dance and Music:**
 
 
• The Bihu dance is a joyous and energetic form of dance performed by young men and women.
 
• The music accompanying the dance is characterized by the use of traditional instruments such as the dhol (drum), pepa (a wind instrument), and gagana (a mouth organ).
 
 
 
• **Community Feasts:**
 
 
• Rongali Bihu is synonymous with community feasts where traditional Assamese dishes such as pitha (rice cakes), larus (sweets made from rice and coconut), and various fish and meat dishes are prepared and enjoyed.
 
• It is a time for families and communities to come together and celebrate with much joy and camaraderie.
 
 
 
• **Symbol of Unity:**
 
 
• Rongali Bihu is not just a festival but a symbol of Assamese unity and identity, bringing people from all walks of life together to celebrate their shared heritage and culture.
